encounters.cc: Routine health maintenance examination with vague somatic complaints

lines: Routine health maintenance examination with vague somatic complaints
She mentions feeling "generally unwell" for the past few months but cannot specify any particular symptoms.
She initially attributes the bruises to being "clumsy" but eventually reveals that her partner has been physically abusive over the past year.
She has not sought help because she fears for her safety and the repercussions from her partner.
She has a history of well-controlled hypothyroidism and no other significant medical history.
Her immunizations are up to date.
She has no history of surgeries
She denies tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drug use.
Her last menstrual period was 3 weeks ago and was normal.
She is sexually active with one male partner and uses condoms inconsistently.
On review of systems, she reports difficulty sleeping and decreased appetite but denies headaches, vision changes, chest pain, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, or changes in bowel habits.
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On physical examination, she appears anxious and has several bruises in different stages of healing on her arms and legs.

lines: Persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating
This 32-year-old female with hypothyroidism on levothyroxine presents two months following her prior encounter where adult physical abuse was identified.
She reports a 6-week history of persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating.
She reports a significant decrease in her appetite and a 5 kg weight loss.
She reports a sleep disturbance, waking up early in the morning and being unable to fall back asleep.
Her family history is significant for bipolar disorder in her uncle.
She denies any history of substance abuse
She denies any thoughts of self-harm or suicide.
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On physical examination, she appears disheveled.
Her thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and complete blood count (CBC) are normal.

encounters.cc: Persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating

lines: Persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating

The patient is a 32-year-old female with hypothyroidism on levothyroxine replacement who returns for ongoing psychiatric management following previous evaluations in March and July 2020, with a known history of physical abuse earlier this year.
She presents with a 6-month history of persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating.
She reports a decreased appetite and unintentional weight loss of 5 kg over the last 4 months.
She was started on sertraline 50 mg daily 3 weeks ago, with no significant improvement in her symptoms.
She is frustrated and inquires about alternative treatment options.
Her family history is significant for depression in her mother.
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On physical examination, she appears tearful with a blunted affect.
Laboratory studies reveal normal thyroid function tests and a normal complete blood count.
